Hey everyone!

I wanted to take a second to introduce myself and discuss a few ideas for the forum.

First off, I'm very excited to be modding for /v/gaming! I believe that a healthy game forum is critical for a site like Voat and I'm excited to be a part of it's fledgling stage. I'm very passionate about gaming and I think this can be an amazing place for us to come together and examine/celebrate/discuss everything we want to about our hobby.

A little about myself: I'm a long time lurker that, in the past year, has decided to drop that status. Playing, writing about and discussing video games used to be a big part of my life when I was younger. I grew up reading Nintendo Power, EGM, PlayStation Magazine (both official and unofficial) and Game Informer. Back then I was inspired by the "hype writers" of the time, people like Dan Shoe and Seanbaby. They promoted the hobby that I loved and helped spread that passion to people like me.

I feel appalled at the state of games media today and I think it sucks that kids don't get to have the experience that I did...but of course, times change and I'm not advocating that we go back there. I'm just trying to give you an idea of why I'm here right now. I'm hoping we can make this a place for positive change for our hobby, and a place for people to express themselves without over moderation or censorship, something that is currently very lacking throughout games forums webwide. And NO I'm not advocating this place to be a hugbox either! Maybe just "real".

Next, I've also created another subverse. This one is /v/moddelete, it's a place for moderators to post deleted content and to give a reason why it was deleted. /v/moddelete is not for obvious spam, illegal content or troll posts; so don't get upset if everything that is deleted isn't posted. It's for things that don't fit on the board for some reason or another (I think we should decide together what that entails soon). I don't imagine I'll be deleting much (hopefully) but I encourage you to subscribe. I will only be moderating these two subs.

Next, I'll be posting meta discussion topics soon as to what kind of content is appropriate for the board. We need to decide "What is Gaming Related", "Guidelines for 'Controversial' and 'Content Creator' Posts" and any other topics you want to.

Finally I'll be posting a date for the "State of the Subverse Mega Thread" soon, it's a thread for everyone to come here and have a discussion about how the board is going and mod performance.

Anyways, that's all I have for now (I'm off to play some Far Cry 4....I will beat this game!)! Please feel free to give me any suggestions, feedback or anything that will help make this sub a good place for everyone!

If your interested in more of my thoughts on /v/gaming, check out my proposal here. Cheers, Devoinz

tl;dr: check out /v/moddelete for deleted posts, be ready to discuss guidelines for the board soon and give me any suggestions or feedback that you have. Edit: Proposal link

Hi /v/code! Here's another classic coding problem:

Given an array of integers, return the maximum contiguous subsequence sum. A contiguous subsequence is simply an unbroken sequence of the elements of the array.

Example input: [2, -6, 3, 5, -1 4]

Example output: 11

Reason: The maximum contiguous subsequence sum comes from [3, 5, -1, 4], which sums to 11.

I've included an untested solution in the comments (not sure it's right). Feel free to add your own solution, even if it's identical. Cheers!
The maximum continuous subsequence sum problem

Potential solution in python:

# Running time: linear. Additional memory requirements: constant
def max_subsequence(arr):
 # The max subsequence sum we've seen so far. Default 0 for 0 elements.
 max_all = 0
 # The max subsequence sum that must include the previous element.
 max_prev = 0

 for elem in arr:
 # We have two choices at each element: include the previous element's
 # max subsequence in our current computation, or start fresh
 max_prev = max(max_prev + elem, elem)
 # Update the maximum possible subsequence.
 max_all = max(max_all, max_prev)

 return max_all

Here's solution in ruby its not the most efficient but it works.

def replace_max(max_ary, new_ary)
 sum = 0
 new_ary.each{|x| sum += x}
 new_ary.push(sum)

 if(max_ary[-1] > new_ary[-1])
 return max_ary
 end
 return new_ary
end

def find_max_con(ary)
 max = []
 sum = 0
 ary.each{|x| sum += x}
 max = ary.dup
 max.push(sum)

 sub_arrays = []
 sub_arrays.push(ary)

 sub_arrays.each do |x|
 if(x.length > 1)
 #trim left
 sub_arrays.push(x[0..-2].dup)

 #trim right
 sub_arrays.push(x[1..-1].dup)
 end
 end

 sub_arrays.each do |x|
 max = replace_max(max.dup, x.dup)
 end
 sub_arrays
 max
end

From Coffee Meets Bagel: 7 times people tend to break up

Are there any tips I should know about how men live that can lead to more peaceful cohabitation?

Everyone is different, so unless he absolutely conforms to gender normative stereotypes (I assume he is a 3-dimensional dynamic person), there really isn't anything specifically on that.

In general, establishing healthy boundaries is essential for a healthy cohabitating romantic relationship. As someone said already about cleaning up accessories etc, so too does it go for all possessions. If he leaves his stuff around, you're not going to want to touch it since you won't know where he likes to put it. So, agreeing on tidiness, chores, finances (specifically shared ones like groceries), how much time each person needs to themselves (e.g. you have a night out with friends on Saturday and he does the same, or one of you stays home to enjoy some alone time), transportation, expectations of how to be considerate around the house, etc.

In fact, you might have a discussion about expectations. As my SO always asks me when unsure of how to help or what to do, "what are your expectations of me?" It's a good starting place.

For example, the common joke for men is that when a woman moves in, he should buy way more toilet paper.
